title: The physiological network reconfigures across sleep stages: time-delay-stability network physiology on real polysomnography

dataset.name: Sleep-EDF Database Expanded (sleep-cassette)
dataset.version: PhysioNet sleep-edfx, subject SC4001 (one overnight PSG)
dataset.record: one overnight polysomnogram: EEG Fpz-Cz (-> delta/alpha/sigma band-power nodes), EOG horizontal, EMG submental, oro-nasal respiration (6 physiological nodes) at 1 Hz over the ~6.7 h scored sleep period, with the expert hypnogram grouped into Wake / Light (N1+N2) / Deep (N3+N4) / REM
dataset.citation: Kemp B, Zwinderman AH, Tuk B, Kamphuisen HAC, Oberye JJL. Analysis of a sleep-dependent neuronal feedback loop. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2000;47(9):1185-1194 (Sleep-EDF, PhysioNet). Network-physiology framework: Bashan A, Bartsch RP, Kantelhardt JW, Havlin S, Ivanov PC. Network physiology reveals relations between network topology and physiological function. Nat Commun 2012;3:702.

proposition: Network physiology treats the body as a network of interacting organ systems and asks how that network REORGANISES with physiological state. Building a 6-node time-delay-stability (TDS) network from one real overnight polysomnogram -- three cortical rhythms (EEG delta/alpha/sigma) plus eye movement, muscle tone and respiration -- and splitting it by sleep stage, the ecosystem reproduces the field's signature finding: the network reconfigures across sleep stages. It is most integrated in REM (11 surrogate-significant links, density 0.73) and least in wake and light sleep (9 links, 0.60); the slow-wave EEG delta rhythm is the persistent hub (highest total degree, 18); and the link set itself turns over -- 6 of 15 possible couplings differ between wake and REM (e.g. respiration engages the network in deep sleep and REM but decouples in light sleep). Only couplings exceeding a phase-randomised surrogate threshold are kept, so the links are the stable, significant ones.

claims.statement: sleep-stage networks compared (Wake / Light / Deep / REM)
surrogate-significant TDS links in REM (the most-integrated state)
REM network density (fraction of the 15 possible links)
couplings that CHANGE between wake and REM (network reconfiguration, of 15)
the network hub (highest total degree across stages) is the EEG delta rhythm (1=yes)

validation.reference: The network-physiology framework (Bashan et al., Nat Commun 2012; Ivanov & Bartsch) establishes that the network of physiological interactions REORGANISES with sleep stage -- coupling topology is state-dependent, not fixed. A correct implementation must (1) recover DIFFERENT networks per sleep stage (density and link set change), (2) keep only surrogate-significant couplings, and (3) show physiologically sensible structure. The ecosystem reproduces this: density varies by stage (REM 0.73 > Deep 0.67 > Light = Wake 0.60), 6/15 links turn over between wake and REM, and the slow-wave delta rhythm is the persistent hub.
validation.data: REAL -- Sleep-EDF Expanded (PhysioNet sleep-edfx), one overnight polysomnogram (subject SC4001) with the expert hypnogram
validation.note: The reproducible finding is the sleep-stage-dependent RECONFIGURATION of the physiological network (density + link set change; REM most integrated; EEG-delta hub), computed with surrogate-thresholded TDS. HONEST scope: (1) SINGLE subject, single night -- the reconfiguration (that the network changes with stage) is the robust, established phenomenon; the exact link counts (9/9/10/11) and density values are subject/night-specific, not universal constants. (2) The surrogate threshold + link counts are DETERMINISTIC given the fixed seed (seed=1, 30 phase-randomised surrogates); a different seed shifts the threshold and can move counts near it by +/-1. (3) Nodes are three EEG band-powers + EOG/EMG/respiration variance at 1 Hz; no ECG is in the sleep-cassette montage, so heart is not a node. (4) TDS windows are 60 s (30 s step, max lag 8 s), the standard network-physiology scale. (5) Stages N1+N2 are pooled as Light and N3+N4 as Deep.

open_questions.q: A group-level analysis across the sleep-edfx cohort (many subjects/nights), a full brain-organ montage including ECG-derived heart rate, and the directed/lagged link structure (who leads whom) would turn the single-subject demonstration into a population network-physiology result. Documented, not escalated.
